proposal.hypothesis: The selected parent combines four shared warp partials with two 64-bit warp-shuffle stages. Summing the four partials directly from shared memory in lane zero may remove those shuffle instructions, while trading them for four serial shared loads and a lane-zero-only branch. This tests a distinct final-aggregation path without changing the 128-thread mapping, one-element-per-lane input, recursive passes, or single CTA barrier; no speedup is assumed.

retained: Replace the final four-partial warp shuffle combination with a lane-zero-only sequential sum of the four shared warp partials after the existing CTA barrier.

Keep 64-bit per-lane and recursive intermediate accumulation, 128 threads, one input element per lane, recursive ceil(count/128) passes, caller-provided scratch, default-stream launches, and final asynchronous device-to-device copy.
